faqs.question: What is the difference between a shayari and a sher?
faqs.answer: Shayari is the general word for Hindi–Urdu poetry; a sher is one two-line unit of it, ending on a shared rhyme (qafiya) and often a repeated word (radif). Most Diwali shayari people forward is either a single sher or a four-line verse.

faqs.question: Can I send these Diwali shayari as if I wrote them?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 12 couplets on this page were written for it, so copy, edit and sign them as your own message. Only the two Nazir Akbarabadi couplets need his name attached.

faqs.question: Who wrote the line 'eent eent par Diwali hai'?
faqs.answer: Nazir Akbarabadi, the Agra poet who lived from 1735 to 1830. It comes from one of his three Diwali poems, printed in the Nazir Granthavali (Uttar Pradesh Hindi Sansthan, 1992).

faqs.question: Is Nazir Akbarabadi's Diwali poetry out of copyright?
faqs.answer: Yes. He died in 1830, so his poems are in the public domain and can be quoted in a card or post. Credit him by name; a modern edition's notes and translations may still be in copyright, so quote only his lines.

faqs.question: Is a four-line Diwali verse still shayari?
faqs.answer: Loosely, yes, but strictly it is a qita or a rhymed greeting rather than a sher. A sher is two lines, which matters on a phone: 48.3% of the pages shared on SubhSandesh are opened on one (measured September 2026).

faqs.question: Should I send Diwali shayari in Hindi script or in English letters?
faqs.answer: Devanagari for people who read Hindi every day, Roman letters for anyone who speaks Hindi or Urdu but types in English, and an English gloss only alongside one of those. Every couplet on this page carries all three.

faqs.question: Which Diwali shayari suits a Jain or Sikh friend?
faqs.answer: Pick one that names no single deity, such as the couplet that sets Lakshmi Puja beside Mahavira's nirvana. Jains mark Mahavira's nirvana and Sikhs mark Bandi Chhor Divas on the same night, which in 2027 is Friday 29 October.

faqs.question: Is it okay to use Urdu words in a Diwali shayari?
faqs.answer: Yes. Shayari has always been written in shared Hindustani, and Nazir Akbarabadi, a Muslim poet, wrote three Diwali poems in it in the 18th century. Swap a word like qubool for a plain Hindi one only if the reader is an elder who prefers formal Hindi.

faqs.question: What Diwali shayari works for someone living abroad?
faqs.answer: Pick a couplet about distance rather than the puja, such as the one about the new moon falling at a different hour in their city. Read it aloud on a video call at their evening, not yours.

faqs.question: Can I put a shayari inside a SubhSandesh Diwali card?
faqs.answer: Yes. The happy-diwali card has a wish on each diya and a letter sealed in a shagun liffafa, and each can hold a couplet; the AI can also draft from a short story. It opens from a private link in any phone browser with no app or account.

faqs.question: How do I write my own Diwali shayari?
faqs.answer: Pick a rhyme word and a repeated ending for both lines, such as maaf rahen and saaf rahen. Put the wish, the name or the twist in the second line, then read it aloud to check it fits one breath.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Shayari: 12 Original Couplets in Hindi, Roman and English

Diwali shayari works best as a single sher: two rhymed lines you can read in one glance on a phone. That matters because 48.3% of the pages people share on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and on Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we hold data for (n = 89 pages, a rough analogue), 49.4% of greetings were built on the day itself. A couplet you can copy in ten seconds on 29 October 2027 beats a 12-line poem nobody finishes.

Below: 12 original sher in Devanagari, Roman and English, grouped by recipient, two public-domain couplets by Nazir Akbarabadi, and when a shayari is wrong.

## What is a Diwali shayari, and what makes it a sher?

A sher is a two-line verse in Hindi–Urdu poetry, and a Diwali shayari is a sher about the festival. John T. Platts's 1884 dictionary defines [sher as "poetry, verse; a verse, a couplet"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%B4%D8%B9%D8%B1&searchhws=yes); each line is a *misra*.

The ending makes it a sher. The *qafiya* is the rhyme, and the *radif* is the repeated word after it, which Platts calls ["independent words placed after the rhyme at the end of hemistichs"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%B1%D8%AF%DB%8C%D9%81&searchhws=yes). In *maaf rahen / saaf rahen* below, *maaf* and *saaf* are the qafiya and *rahen* the radif.

In the India top 10 we checked on 22 October 2026, both news listicles printed mostly four-line verses instead. Those are closer to a *qita* than a sher.

## 12 original Diwali shayari, grouped by who receives them

Every line was written for this page. Diwali 2027 falls on Friday 29 October.

### 1. For parents

Use *aap* or *Papa*, and lean on memory, not prosperity. Send on 29 October, before the puja.

> माँ के हाथ की बाती अब भी उतनी ही सीधी जलती है,\
मैं कितना भी दूर रहूँ, दिवाली उसी आँगन से चलती है।\
*Maa ke haath ki baati ab bhi utni hi seedhi jalti hai, main kitna bhi door rahoon, Diwali usi aangan se chalti hai.*\
Mother's wick still burns straight; however far I live, Diwali starts from that courtyard.

> पापा, इस बार भी छत पर पहली लड़ी आप ही लगाइएगा,\
हम बस सीढ़ी थामेंगे, बाक़ी हुनर आप ही दिखाइएगा।\
*Papa, is baar bhi chhat par pehli ladi aap hi lagaiyega, hum bas seedhi thaamenge, baaqi hunar aap hi dikhaiyega.*\
Papa, you hang the first string of lights on the roof again; we will only hold the ladder.

### 2. For a partner or spouse

Use *tum*, and let Urdu words like *mashghool* (busy) and *qubool* (accepted) carry the romance. Send late on 29 October.

> तुम्हारी हँसी से पहले इस घर में कोई दिया पूरा नहीं जलता,\
रंगोली भी अधूरी लगती है जब तक तुम्हारा रंग नहीं मिलता।\
*Tumhaari hansi se pehle is ghar mein koi diya poora nahin jalta, rangoli bhi adhoori lagti hai jab tak tumhaara rang nahin milta.*\
Until you laugh, no diya here burns fully; even the rangoli waits for your colour.

> सारा शहर आज रौशनी गिनने में मशग़ूल है,\
मुझे तो बस तुम्हारी आँखों का एक दिया क़बूल है।\
*Saara shahar aaj raushni ginne mein mashghool hai, mujhe to bas tumhaari aankhon ka ek diya qubool hai.*\
The city is busy counting its lights; the only diya I accept is the one in your eyes.

### 3. For friends

Use *tum* or *tu*, and joke. Send any time on 29 October.

> तेरे हिस्से की काजू कतली अब तक डिब्बे में बची है,\
सोन पापड़ी तो हर साल की तरह आगे बढ़ चुकी है।\
*Tere hisse ki kaju katli ab tak dibbe mein bachi hai, son papdi to har saal ki tarah aage badh chuki hai.*\
Your share of kaju katli is still in the box; the soan papdi, as every year, has been passed on.

> साल भर के झगड़े आज की रात माफ़ रहें,\
दिये की लौ की तरह दोस्ती के इरादे साफ़ रहें।\
*Saal bhar ke jhagde aaj ki raat maaf rahen, diye ki lau ki tarah dosti ke iraade saaf rahen.*\
Let a year of quarrels be forgiven tonight; like a diya's flame, let our friendship stay clear.

### 4. For someone far away

For anyone in another city or country. The new moon falls at a different local hour abroad, which the first sher uses.

> तुम जिस शहर में हो, वहाँ अमावस भी शायद अलग होगी,\
पर जो दिया मैं यहाँ रखूँगा, उसकी लौ तुम तक भी पहुँचेगी।\
*Tum jis shahar mein ho, wahaan amaavas bhi shaayad alag hogi, par jo diya main yahaan rakhoonga, uski lau tum tak bhi pahunchegi.*\
The new-moon night may differ in your city; the flame of the diya I place here will still reach you.

> घर की थाली में इस बार एक कटोरी ख़ाली रहेगी,\
तेरे लौटने तक हर दिवाली थोड़ी सवाली रहेगी।\
*Ghar ki thaali mein is baar ek katori khaali rahegi, tere lautne tak har Diwali thodi savaali rahegi.*\
One bowl on the family thali stays empty; until you return, every Diwali asks a small question.

For one person far away, a sher alone is a thin gift. SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card on the happy-diwali page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) puts a line on each wish diya, seals a letter in a shagun liffafa and holds up to six photos, from a private link. For a partner you miss all year, the [miss-you page with open-when letters](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better; 92.1% of its senders add at least one.

### 5. For a brother or sister, on Bhai Dooj

Use *tu* and tease. Bhai Dooj is Sunday 31 October 2027.

> बचपन में मेरा अनार तू पहले जला देता था,\
आज भी भाई दूज पर आधी मिठाई तू ही ले लेता है।\
*Bachpan mein mera anaar tu pehle jala deta tha, aaj bhi Bhai Dooj par aadhi mithaai tu hi le leta hai.*\
As kids you lit my anaar first; even now, on Bhai Dooj, you take half the sweets.

> दीदी, तेरी रंगोली के बिना आँगन अब भी अधूरा है,\
तू ससुराल में दिया जलाए, तो यहाँ उजाला पूरा है।\
*Didi, teri rangoli ke bina aangan ab bhi adhoora hai, tu sasuraal mein diya jalaaye, to yahaan ujaala poora hai.*\
Didi, without your rangoli the courtyard feels unfinished; when you light a diya at your in-laws', the light here is whole.

### 6. For a group or a mixed office

Name no single deity: the night is Lakshmi Puja for some, Mahavira's nirvana or Bandi Chhor Divas for others. Send on 28 October.

> कोई लक्ष्मी पूजे, कोई महावीर का निर्वाण मनाए,\
अमावस की इस रात हर घर अपने ढंग से दिया जलाए।\
*Koi Lakshmi pooje, koi Mahavir ka nirvaan manaaye, amaavas ki is raat har ghar apne dhang se diya jalaaye.*\
One home worships Lakshmi, another marks Mahavira's nirvana; tonight every home lights its diya its own way.

> साल भर की थकान आज दरवाज़े पर ही उतार देना,\
कल फिर मिलेंगे, आज की रात बस घर को दे देना।\
*Saal bhar ki thakaan aaj darwaaze par hi utaar dena, kal phir milenge, aaj ki raat bas ghar ko de dena.*\
Leave the year's tiredness at the door; we meet again soon, so give tonight to home.

## Nazir Akbarabadi's Diwali: two classical couplets to quote

[Nazir Akbarabadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazeer_Akbarabadi) (1735–1830) wrote three Diwali poems in Agra, now public domain. Both lines are from the [*Nazir Granthavali* (Uttar Pradesh Hindi Sansthan, 1992), pp. 370–378, on archive.org](https://archive.org/details/nazir-granthavali-by-nazir-akbarabadi-edited-by-dr-nazir-muhammad-1); credit him by name.

> हमें अदाएँ दिवाली की ज़ोर भाती हैं,\
कि लाखों झमकें हर एक घर में जगमगाती हैं।\
*Hamein adaayen Diwali ki zor bhaati hain, ki laakhon jhamken har ek ghar mein jagmagaati hain.*\
Diwali's ways delight me hugely, for lakhs of sparkles glitter in every house. (Nazir Akbarabadi, "Diwali-3")

> जिधर को देखो उधर रोशनी उजाली है,\
ग़रज़ मैं क्या कहूँ, ईंट ईंट पर दिवाली है।\
*Jidhar ko dekho udhar raushni ujaali hai, gharaz main kya kahoon, eent eent par Diwali hai.*\
Wherever you look the light is bright; what more can I say, there is Diwali on every brick. (Nazir Akbarabadi, "Diwali-3")

Nazir, a Muslim poet, wrote Diwali as a street festival of toy-sellers, batashe and lamps; stanzas on dice games are left out here. Many famous Diwali couplets online belong to 20th-century poets still in copyright.

## Why the second line of a sher carries the weight

Put the wish, the name or the twist in the second line. A 2017 study in *Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience* by Wassiliwizky and colleagues found that [chills while listening to poetry cluster towards the end of lines, stanzas and whole poems](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5597896), with reward-circuit activity rising just before those closing points.

The sample was 27 German speakers, so treat it as a principle, not proof for Hindi. Hide your second line; if the first already says everything, rewrite.

## Devanagari, Roman or English: which version to send

Send Devanagari to daily Hindi readers, Roman to anyone who types Hindi in English letters, and English only alongside one of them. A 2023 ACL workshop paper by Nielsen, Kirov and Roark notes that [Hindi and Urdu are both widely and informally romanized](https://aclanthology.org/2023.cawl-1.5/) and that language-identification systems typically conflate them, so Roman shayari reaches both audiences. The table compares four formats against what we can measure.

| Format | How it is read | What lasts | SubhSandesh figure (24 Sept 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp text | One message | The chat | 48.3% of page views are on a phone |
| Story image | One screen, 24 hours | The picture | Diwali card saves at 1080×1920 |
| Interactive page | A line per diya, plus a letter | A reopenable link | 11.1 views per created page |
| Printed card | By hand | The paper | Not measured |

A WhatsApp sher is read once; a page is viewed 11.1 times on average across all SubhSandesh page types. No Diwali figure exists yet.

## When a shayari is the wrong Diwali message

A sher is wrong for an elder who reads only formal Hindi, where a plain *shubh Deepavali* does more. It is also wrong for a family in its first year of mourning.

SubhSandesh is the wrong tool for a group of 40: the Diwali page is built for one person. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, 49.4% of pages were built on the day, so keep the afternoon of 29 October free if you want one.

## Sources

- *Nazir Granthavali*, ed. Nazir Muhammad, 1992 — archive.org.
- Platts, *A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English*, 1884 — DSAL.
- Wassiliwizky et al., "The emotional power of poetry", 28 April 2017 — Europe PMC.
- Nielsen, Kirov and Roark, "Distinguishing Romanized Hindi from Romanized Urdu", July 2023 — ACL Anthology.
